correctness.rationale: A direct uniform endpoint expansion of the independent exponential densities gives intensity e^{-u-z} du dz on compact sets; rare event independence proves the limiting Poisson Laplace functional. The global bound (n/k)^alpha>=1+alpha(1-k/n) uniformly controls all omitted far labels above a fixed height. This proves top-point convergence, and factorization implies iid Exp(1) spatial marks independent of top heights and Gumbel maximum. Independent Poisson marking gives exactly the last-label distribution in discrete Zipf sampling; the variance of time depoissonization is bounded by (1+log n)/A_n ->0 with A_n>=n. The executable checker corroborates finite cases; it does not certify the limiting argument.

originality.rationale: Direct comparison with increasing-rate independent exponential maxima, unequal-coupon marginal collector limit theorems, and equal-probability unmarked point processes found no implication of the joint index-location limit for power-Zipf coupons. The new claim is the marked endpoint scaling and independent joint law, not the classical marginal Gumbel limit. A generic Poisson theorem is methodologically related but does not state the precise power-law endpoint geometry.
residual_risks: A general marked triangular-array rare-event Poisson theorem or overlooked coupon-collector paper may already contain an equivalent power-Zipf localization formula.

value.rationale: Power-Zipf coupon models naturally raise which near-rarest type is last. The theorem quantifies a nontrivial endpoint layer of width n/log n, a universal exponential rescaled last rank, its asymptotic independence from completion-time Gumbel fluctuations, and corresponding fixed-top-r marks. This is structural distributional information not contained in existing marginal cover-time limits; an exact additional downstream application is not presumed.
